findingDetails.title: Baseline capture and read paths are not symlink-contained
findingDetails.evidence: captureBaselineFile creates and copies to a path below the lineage baseline directory without canonical or no-follow validation; readBaselineContent later consumes the recorded path without validating ancestry.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The runner passes the lineage directory as the capture root, and the security tests cover quarantine links but no baseline-destination or baseline-read symlink case.
findingDetails.recommendation: Apply canonical/no-follow validation to baseline capture and reads and refuse symlinked ancestors or final components.
findingDetails.claim: A stale or concurrent symlink in the lineage baseline tree can redirect copied dirty bytes outside the artifact or make restore consume bytes from outside the artifact.
counterevidenceSought: destination refusal applied to baseline capture
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The lineage directory is normally private, so exploitation requires a stale attempt artifact or another actor with write access; that is still within the shared fan-out trust boundary.

findingDetails.title: Restore checks only the final component and can follow a symlinked parent
findingDetails.evidence: Tracked restore checks only lstat of the final path before writeFileSync; not-in-HEAD restore also recreates parents and writes without an ancestor no-follow or canonical guard.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both restore branches share the same path-based boundary, while the current security test covers only a final-component symlink.
findingDetails.recommendation: Validate every ancestor and use an atomic no-follow directory/file-handle strategy for both restore branches.
findingDetails.claim: A child or concurrent actor can replace a repository parent directory with a symlink and cause restore bytes to be written outside the repository.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The final-component guard blocks the simplest symlink case, but it does not protect parent-directory substitution that path-based writes follow.

findingDetails.title: Quarantine destination validation is vulnerable to check-then-create replacement
findingDetails.evidence: quarantineDestinationRefusal checks current ancestors, then writeQuarantineFile recursively creates directories and opens the destination by path, leaving a replacement race.
findingDetails.scopeProof: All quarantine payloads and the manifest flow through writeQuarantineFile, so the race applies to the shared destination writer.
findingDetails.recommendation: Anchor quarantine creation to a verified directory handle or equivalent atomic no-follow operation, or lock validation and creation together.
findingDetails.claim: Path-based refusal followed by recursive creation does not establish an atomic no-follow quarantine boundary under concurrent writes.
counterevidenceSought: serialized writer lock covering check and create
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A private single-writer lineage lowers race likelihood, but concurrent fan-out lanes and shared containment artifacts keep the invariant relevant.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: The security boundary spans trusted evidence writes, restore writes, concurrent fan-out, and focused regression tests.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Selected every producer and consumer of baseline, quarantine, and restore bytes plus the security requirement and tests.
